articleTitle: Dual-Band Vivaldi MIMO Antennas Designed for Sub-6 GHz 5G Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system was designed for Sub-6 GHz 5G wireless applications using a Vivaldi shape. The proposed antenna consists of two Vivaldi elements designed to operate in the 3.3-3.8 GHz and 4.8-5.0 GHz frequency bands, which are allocated for 5G communications. The antenna is designed on an FR4 substrate with a compact size of 120 mm 120 mm. The antenna elements are optimized to achieve good impedance matching, high gain, and low mutual coupling within the desired frequency bands. The simulated and measured results demonstrate that the proposed antenna exhibits a reflection coefficient below -10 dB, mutual coupling less than -25 dB, realized gain greater than 6.13 dBi, and envelope correlation coefficient below 0.01 in the operating bands, indicating its suitability for MIMO applications. The experimental measurements show a satisfactory agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Modeling and Characterization of a Compact In-Line Filter with Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative method for generating transmission zeros within a circuit model, eliminating the necessity for extra resonators. It capitalizes on employing posts within a cavity to produce transmission zeros, thereby improving selectivity without enlarging the overall size of the circuit. Through this approach, precise control over the positioning of transmission zeros becomes achievable. The process commences with the development of a single resonator, and then progresses to crafting a third-order filter with a bandwidth of 400 MHz, focused at 3 GHz. This novel framework bears significant implications for the creation of compact and effective filters in high-frequency applications, promising enhanced efficiency and performance.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Traffic Characteristics of Elastic Optical Networks Nodes with Priority-Based Call Admission Control Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: The impact on the traffic characteristics of current telecommunications networks is a very important issue from the point of view of high load and, consequently, optimal use of resources. The article presents an analysis of the traffic characteristics of elastic optical network (EON) nodes in which the structure of a 3-stage Clos switching network was used. The results of the loss probability and average resource utilization of the output directions are obtained using a simulator developed and implemented by the authors.

articleTitle: Navigating the Future: Digital Twin in Maritime Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: This paper presents the idea of Digital Twins, a novel technology that allows previously unheard-of degrees of simulation, analysis, and control by reflecting actual objects into their digital equivalents. The article starts by giving a thorough overview of digital twins and outlining their diverse kinds, such as prescriptive, descriptive, and predictive models, each of which has a specific function in a variety of businesses. The emphasis switches to how Digital Twins might be used in the maritime industry, namely in port operations. The study examines how real-time data analysis, predictive maintenance, and operational optimization provided by digital twins may transform port management, logistics, safety, and environmental sustainability. Furthermore, it goes into more detail about the processes involved in building Digital Twins, emphasizing the incorporation of machine learning, simulation, data analytics, and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors. Together, these techniques help to accurately replicate physical assets in a virtual environment, which promotes improved decisionmaking. Additionally, there are described several software platforms that can be used to create Digital Twins with their features, interoperability, and integration potential. Software that facilitates the production of Digital Twins and offers schematic views for complex visualization and interaction with the digital models receives particular attention. Essentially, the goal of this article is to clarify how Digital Twins are revolutionizing port operations by providing an understanding of their creation process and the technology that enables it. Through this investigation there are highlighted the major advantages and challenges of implementing Digital Twins in ports, such as increased productivity, decreased operating expenses, and a proactive approach to sustainability and maintenance issues.

articleTitle: Measurement of a Baby Dummy in a Car for Child Presence Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: The range of applications for ultra-wideband (UWB) radar has been expanding in recent years. Detecting living objects, humans or animals, in a static environment is an interesting application. After a natural disaster, locating people under ruins is a life-saving application. However, the automotive sector has also found usage for UWB radars. Remind the driver of children or pets locked in car and left behind. Also observing the driver's vital function and alert the rescue in case of emergency is a major use-case. It is particularly challenging to detect infants in a car within a short period of time. Compared to adults, a lack of measurement data exists for infants. In this paper we present a statistical analysis of measurements inside a car with a baby dummy.

articleTitle: Deploying DAPHNE Computational Intelligence on EuroHPC Vega for Benchmarking Randomised Optimisation Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: This paper presents a deployment of DAPHNE (Integrated Data Analysis Pipelines for Large-Scale Data Management, HPC and Machine Learning) for Computational Intelligence (CI). As CI progresses, e.g. through effort in human societies like the IEEE Computational Intelligence Society (CIS), the latest advances have become more widely popularized. Likewise, with the accessibility of supercomputing resources to advance CI, like with infrastructures such as EuroHPC machines including Vega, this paper demonstrates deployment of Randomised Optimisation Algorithms (ROAs) as a subset of CI algorithms, on EuroHPC Vega. As the Vega is a cluster of distributed nodes, a successful computation on several nodes at once in parallel and concurrently, requires an orchestrated deployment across the nodes, batched using Slurm in this paper. An example ROA benchmarking scenario is then presented in this scope.

articleTitle: From Concept to Implementation: Lessons Learned in Designing and Deploying a Visible Light Positioning System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Visible Light Positioning (VLP) systems offer a sophisticated solution to achieve indoor positioning. Utilizing the existing LED (light emitting diode) lighting infrastructure along with an optical receiver, the position of an object or an individual can be determined. In this work we give an overview of the design process of our own VLP system with the goal of creating an easily adoptable VLP system that utilizes conventional LED light and design a compact optical receiver unit for it. We demonstrate how frequency modulated LEDs, enable LED identification for the applied positioning algorithm, while remaining unobtrusive to room occupants. This work is intended to give reasoning to our design choices and to project future enhancements for the VLP system, both in terms of software and hardware.

articleTitle: Modified Mikaelian Lens for RF Applications Using Metamaterials and Modern 3D Printing Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: This paper will discuss the design and modeling of the Mikaelian gradient index lens for 5.8GHz. We aimed to improve the lens' performance while utilizing cost-effective materials. We used ABS-like filament, which can easily be 3D printed making the manufacturing cost-effective. One of the key elements that make our lens stand out is that it has a cross-shaped single-cell structure. Also, we made modifications to the shape of the lens and to the layer-to-layer change of refractive index that improved the lens' performance. The article also explains the calculation behind the structure.

articleTitle: Designing an Augmented Reality Teaching Module for Power Consumption in FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) are electronic devices that are being increasingly used because of their programming features and advantage to fulfil the required technical specifications of the designs. Augmented Reality (AR) is a technology widely used especially for educational purposes due to its potential applications in various fields. In this paper, we explore the utilization of AR in the context of power consumption techniques for FPGAs. Furthermore, this work presents the integration of AR technology to better visualize and analyze FPGA power consumption techniques. By using animations, students can gain insights into power consumption patterns and optimization techniques for FPGA-based designs. We present a framework for AR-enhanced FPGA power consumption monitoring and analysis during the implementation process, and demonstrate its effectiveness through experimental results. The results show the potential of AR technology to enhance the understanding and management of FPGA power consumption, overlaying the way for more efficient system design practices.

articleTitle: Optimal Energy Management for Grid-Connected Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: In this paper, optimal energy management in a grid-connected microgrid including a three-phase load of a small group of houses, a PV system, a proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) stack, a battery energy storage system (BESS), and an energy management system (EMS) is considered. A classical proportional-integral (PI) control strategy for BESS is applied. Optimization of the operating schedules of the PEMFC stack and the BESS was performed using a MATLAB solver. In this way, the load on the PEMFC is minimized and the system's life time is extended. The presented approach is promising. Validation of the results using simulation of the microgrid operation in MATLAB (Simulink and SimPowerSystems toolboxes) is possible.

articleTitle: AI in PCB Design: Insights from a Focused Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Printed Circuit Board (PCB) design tools, highlighting the transformative impact AI can have on PCB design workflows. Based on the available documentation and secondary sources, nine AI-powered PCB design tools are analyzed, with a discussion of their features, strengths, and limitations. Due to access constraints, only Flux.ai was tested directly, serving as a focused case study. The case study demonstrates the capabilities of Flux.ai's AI Copilot feature, while also acknowledging its limitations. Our findings advocate for a future where AI-driven design tools enhance efficiency, precision, and user-friendliness in PCB design, setting new benchmarks for the field.

articleTitle: Transmission Line-Based Wave Digital Approach for $N-\text{way}$ Bagley Power Dividers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: This paper explores the degrees of freedom of previously suggested transmission line (TL)-based wave digital (WD) approach. It shows the flexibility of using the WD modelling approach for any power ratio in case of multi-way Bagley power divider. Validation of the implemented WD models against analytical solutions and measurements of the physical microstrip circuits is done to ensure accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimisation of Resource Allocation in 5G Network for Critical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Given the swift pace of technological advancement, wireless networks are assuming an ever more crucial role in the world around us. Access networks, facilitating users' access to resources such as the Internet, now extend beyond home or public WiFi networks to encompass mobile networks as well. This is particularly evident in the case of the latest two generations, namely 4G (LTE) and 5G networks. Offering higher data transmission speeds compared to earlier iterations of mobile networks, and meeting stringent Quality of Service requirements, mobile networks can serve as vital components of critical infrastructure, particularly in domains such as public safety, where they may be integrated into life-saving systems. The article proposes a solution aimed at bolstering the functionality of 5G networks within such systems. The efficacy of this solution is validated through results obtained via the proposed analytical model and digital simulations.

articleTitle: Digital Twins to Monitor IoT Devices for Green Transformation of University Campus
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: In recent years, IoT devices have become increasingly prevalent in various sectors, including higher education institutions. Traditional university campus management is facing problems such as high cost, difficult maintenance, low efficiency, energy waste and so on. The construction of smart university campuses is the inevitable trend of the development of universities. However managing and optimizing IoT devices pose significant challenges due to their diverse nature and complex interactions. Digital twin technology offers a promising solution by providing virtual representations of physical objects and environments, enabling real-time monitoring of IoT devices for optimizing various aspects of university campus. The proposed model is positioned as one of the most cost-effective methods available for automation, turning a regular lecture hall into a smart and efficient one. The aim of this paper is to enhance the overall experience of administrators for campus management by gaining insights into campus operations, by providing complete remote control and automation of HVAC systems, including streamlined remote control based on building the digital twin of the physical prototype and monitoring it on real time mode leading to reduced energy consumption.

articleTitle: Joint Communication and Sensing Prospects: Potential Through Visible Light
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Joint Communication and Sensing (JCS) emerges as a crucial technology composed to revolutionize forthcoming wireless systems. Acknowledged as both a vital technology and a pivotal usage scenario for the anticipated 6th generation (6G) wireless networks, JCS takes advantages of the communication signals to detect and as well monitor the surrounding environment, facilitating sensing, target detection, and localization. However, current JCS technologies meet various challenges demanding comprehensive solutions. These challenges include standardization, privacy, security, interference, energy efficiency, complexity and cost. Advancements in technologies supporting JCS facilitate the seamless integration of sensing and communication capabilities. Key technologies contributing to JCS include visible light communication, millimeter-wave communication, radar systems, sensor fusion and machine learning. This manuscript discusses the fundamental elements of JCS, various approaches, current challenges and prospects for future contributions with particular focus on Radio Frequency RF-JCS, as well as the widely adopted innovative approach based on Visible Light technologies VL-JCS, which promises to contribute significantly to the future of JCS research.

articleTitle: From Ray Tracing to Channel Impulse Responses: A Review on the Description of Polarimetric Time-Invariant SISO Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: One key enabler of autonomous driving is vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication and positioning using cellular technologies. To design a vehicular localization system, the understanding and modeling of the physical radio channel (RC) is crucial. Polarization is an important yet often overlooked parameter of the RC. The combined polarization of the transmitting and receiving antennas, along with the environment, significantly affects the Channel Impulse Response (CIR) and localization performance. This paper aims to provide a deterministic description of the time-invariant Single-Input Single-Output (SISO) RC with focus on its polarimetric properties. The aim is to link the understanding of physical wave propagation directly to the conventional CIR descriptions used in localization and signal processing. The focus is on SISO RC modeling for arbitrary antennas, including Line-of-Sight (LoS) and multiple reflections. This study intentionally excludes diffraction, diffuse scattering, and bandwidth limitations, yet establishes a foundational frame-work for future multi-antenna systems with full polarimetric capabilities. The paper describes wave propagation using the Jones Calculus to separate polarimetric wave components, and models the polarimetric reception typical of RC modeling methods in positioning. This approach allows for the calculation of received signal at the antenna feed point. The application context of this research is in ranging or positioning within the V2X framework.

articleTitle: Dimensioning Challenges of Telecommunication Network Elements Migrating Onto the Cloud (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: The excursion on the long road of telecommunications is continuously evolving. Newer mobile generations, optimizations, modernizations, technology changes, and various mergers have been experienced in the past decades. Different drivers continuously shift physical network elements towards software (SW) only deployments in all IP telecommunication networks. The decoupling of application SW from hardware (HW) is accelerated by virtualization. The ‘cloudification’ of legacy telecommunication equipment made communication networks not only more flexible, but also opened new doors. Brand new services became available thanks to the ongoing fusion of two domains: telecommunications and IT (Information Technology). A new era called ‘Telco-Cloud’ was born. One original goal was to use commercial IT computing servers as HW platform hoping cost efficiency. Another expected benefit was the prompt use of existing experience in the operation and maintenance of IT HW in Data Centers. More and more network functions are virtualized on top of IT HW nowadays. However, the strict requirements of the legacy-Physical Network Function (PNF) based-telecommunications mandate special configurations and practices on cloud. The rapidly increasing amount of Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) and Cloud-native Network Functions (CNFs) introduces new concepts for dimensioning, deployment, operation, management, and monitoring. Some availability and operability requirements and expectations are inherited from the legacy PNF domain, meanwhile the telecommunication world itself undergoes a continuous change towards Telco-Cloud and 5G/6G. This paper overviews the evolution steps to Telco-Cloud. The challenges in the dimensioning and availability design are discussed, and some concepts and examples are presented on NF and network levels.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification and Variance-Based Sensitivity Analysis for Microstrip Line on IC-Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: In this paper, we present numerical uncertainty quantification using polynomial chaos expansion and variance-based global sensitivity analysis of a microstrip fabricated on IC-substrates. Microstrip design parameters such as line width, trace height, substrate thickness, relative dielectric constant, and loss tangent are assumed to have Gaussian probability distribution depending on IC-substrate manufacturing processes. Those input parameter variations are represented by orthogonal polynomials and their coefficients. The impact of the varied design input parameters on the electrical characteristics such as a characteristic impedance and propagation constant is quantitatively analyzed. For computational efficiency, non-intrusive spectral projection method with Smolyak sparse grid technique is employed to mitigate the numerical multi-dimensional integration. Variance-based sensitivity analysis using Sobol indices is also performed for the investigation of significant input parameters on each output parameter at several frequencies.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Time Synchronization Solution for the Bistatic Synthetic Aperture Radar Using Mobile Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems play an important role in the fields of remote sensing and target acquisition. In bistatic radar arrangements, where the transmitter and receiver are situated at separate locations, precise synchronization between these components is crucial to providing high-quality image reconstruction. In this study, an analysis of synchronization methods that utilise accurate timing mechanisms was made. These methods are used to guarantee consistent data collection and processing. Although we await experimental confirmation, this preliminary investigation establishes the foundation for the future advancement of synchronization solutions in BiSAR systems. We also proposed an innovative configuration for an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based BiSAR system and a solution for its time and phase synchronization. While experimental confirmation is still awaited, this initial inquiry lays the groundwork for the future development of synchronization solutions in BiSAR systems.

articleTitle: Advancing Automotive Connectivity: New Technologies and Security Considerations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: The automotive industry is changing from mechanical engineering towards the software-defined vehicle. A modern vehicle contains more software than a common aircraft to implement Advanced Driver Assistance Systems, ADAS. These systems provide road users with advanced safety features such as adaptive cruise control, brake, lane and steer assistant and pave the way toward autonomous vehicles. To realize these functionalities, several connectivity services must be included within a modern vehicle – from backend connectivity, navigation, emergency calls (eCall), traffic assistance, Over-theAir (OTA) updates, all the way to streaming services and Wi-Fi hotspots for passengers. A permanent internet connection must be guaranteed and other communication strategies such as Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V), Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I), Vehicle-to-Cloud (V2C), Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) technologies need to be considered. RF technologies within the ISM and other RF bands are used, and a variety of antennas need to be integrated to provide best possible signal coverage in any driving situation. This paper features a brief description of new automotive technologies, connectivity considerations by antenna simulations and the resultant cyber security concerns that arise from the large number of connections.

articleTitle: An Efficient Algorithm for Scheduling Aircraft Landing Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
abstract: An efficient heuristic algorithm with polynomial computational complexity developed for solving the aircraft static landing problem (ALP) is proposed in this paper. The optimal solution of ALP is considered for the case where a set of aircraft is available for landing. The problem is considered under specific constraints. Three test instances with 10, 20, and 30 landing airplanes were solved. For each of them, three variants were solved: 1) landing on one runway, 2) landing on two runways, and 3) landing on three runways. Optimal solutions were obtained for all test instances. A comparison of the obtained results with those of a genetic algorithm is discussed. The proposed novel algorithm is efficient and can successfully solve larger problems with a larger number of landing aircraft and more runways.

articleTitle: Front Matter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Broadband Communications for Next Generation Networks and Multimedia Applications (CoBCom)
